about: Invented, longer than coined_label_stories.json: the shapes real agent notes, harness sessions and project chats take, where one conversation talks about eight or ten parts of a named project. Same format as the short set; run the same modes with --fixture.

stories.title: Driftwood status
stories.body:
# Driftwood, where things stand

Driftwood is the photo organiser the person is building on weekends.

## Shipped this week
- PR #302: Rework the duplicate finder so near-identical shots are grouped, not deleted
- PR #305: Move thumbnail generation into a background worker
- PR #306: Nightly backup report, sent as a PDF to the person's inbox
- PR #309: Import from the old phone export (zip, 2 GB limit)

## Decisions
- The person wants face tagging off by default; it stays an opt-in setting.
- Albums are plain folders on disk, no database of its own.

## Open
- The map view is slow with more than 5,000 photos.
- First public beta targeted for the 20th, 30 testers.

stories.title: Harbourlight handoff
stories.body: Handoff for Harbourlight (invoicing tool). Done: PR #88 Recurring invoice scheduler; PR #91 Late payment reminder emails; PR #93 Tax summary export for the accountant; PR #95 Currency rounding fix. The person decided to keep the PDF renderer in-house after trying two vendors. Next: the client portal login is half built, the first paying customer starts on the 3rd of next month, and the onboarding checklist still needs copy.

stories.title: Harbourlight notes
stories.body: Harbourlight is the person's invoicing tool for freelancers. It has a recurring invoice scheduler, a late payment reminder flow and a tax summary export. The accountant integration is built on the accountant's CSV format. The person's first paying customer joins next month. The weekly founder digest email is still manual. The person wants the dashboard to show money owed first.

stories.title: Quillgrove feedback
stories.body: Quillgrove is the person's novel-writing tool. Beta readers asked for a distraction-free mode and a way to track which chapters are drafted, revised or final. The person built the chapter status board first, then the comment sidebar for beta readers. The export to EPUB uses a template the person bought. The person says the autosave conflict problem is solved.

stories.title: Driftwood big session
turns: Work on Driftwood today. The thumbnails are slow and the backup report never arrives.

I profiled the thumbnail step: it ran on the main thread. I moved thumbnail generation into a background worker with a bounded queue, which cut a 4,000 photo import from 11 minutes to 3. I also found the backup report job was scheduled in the wrong timezone, fixed that, and changed the report to a PDF with a summary table. Along the way I tidied the settings screen, removed the unused face tagging toggle's default of on, and added a regression test for the duplicate grouping. PR #305 and PR #306 are open.
great. Make face tagging off by default, I never wanted it on. And can you also look at why the map view is so slow with big libraries?

Face tagging is now opt-in. For the map view: it renders every marker at once. I added clustering so only visible markers draw, tested with 6,000 photos, and the map opens in under a second. That is PR #307.
perfect, merge 305 first.

stories.title: Harbourlight reminders
turns: In Harbourlight, the late payment reminders go out on the wrong day when the client is in another timezone.

Fixed. Reminders are now computed in the client's timezone, I added a test for daylight saving changes, and the reminder email now shows the amount and the original due date. I also added a retry when the mail provider returns a temporary error, and renamed the confusing 'dunning' job to 'payment reminders' in the admin screen. PR #96.
nice. Also the accountant export should include the tax id column.
Added the tax id column to the accountant export and a note in the header row; PR #97.
ship both.

stories.title: Mareviva sesion larga
turns: Trabaja en Mareviva: la pantalla de la semana tarda mucho y el aviso de marea baja a veces llega tarde.

Hecho. Movi la carga de la prevision a segundo plano con cache de una hora, corregi el aviso de marea baja para que se calcule con la zona horaria de la playa, anadi un modo sin conexion que muestra la ultima prevision guardada y limpie el onboarding: ahora son tres pantallas. Tambien cambie el nombre del trabajo nocturno de 'sync' a 'prevision diaria'. PR #81 y PR #82.
bien. El onboarding de tres pantallas me gusta. Falta el widget de la pantalla de inicio.
El widget de inicio queda para la proxima sesion; abri una nota en el backlog.

stories.title: Planning the Driftwood beta
turns: I want to plan the Driftwood beta. Thirty testers on the 20th. The things that must work: importing from the old phone export, the duplicate grouping, and the nightly backup report. The map is nice to have. I also want a first-run walkthrough that explains albums are just folders, and a feedback form inside the app.
A sensible order: import first, because every tester starts there. Then the walkthrough, then the feedback form. The backup report can wait until the second week of the beta.
Fine. But I'd rather ship the report in week one, since it is the thing testers will tell friends about. Let's cut the map from the beta entirely and put the feedback form in the settings screen.
Then the beta scope is: import, duplicate grouping, backup report, walkthrough, and a feedback form in settings. The map moves to after the beta.

stories.title: Invoicing tool pricing
turns: Harbourlight pricing: I'm thinking 12 euros a month for solo freelancers, and a team plan at 29. The reminders and the tax export are what people pay for. I'm not sure whether the client portal should be free or part of the team plan. The first customer already said they want the portal for their own clients.
Portals tend to be a team feature. A free portal with a small logo is a common compromise.
I like the logo idea. Free portal with a logo on solo, no logo on the team plan. And for the first customer I'll offer three months free.

stories.title: Brunnwerk Planung
turns: Fuer Brunnwerk plane ich diese Woche drei Dinge: die Mahnungen sollen nach vierzehn Tagen automatisch rausgehen, die Rechnungsvorschau muss schneller werden, und ich will einen Export fuer den Steuerberater bauen. Die Vorschau ist das groesste Problem, sie braucht fuenf Sekunden.
Starte mit der Vorschau: zwischenspeichern und die Bilder verkleinern. Der Export ist dann ein kleiner Schritt.
Gut, Vorschau zuerst, dann der Export, die Mahnungen am Ende.

stories.title: Nota de sesion
stories.body: Nota de la sesion sobre Mareviva. PR #84: widget de la pantalla de inicio. PR #85: aviso de marea baja con la zona horaria de la playa. PR #86: resumen semanal por correo de las mejores olas. La persona decidio no usar un servicio de pronostico externo y mantener su propia fuente. Pendiente: la pagina de ajustes y la guia de primer uso.

stories.title: First project
turns: I'm looking for a good first open source project to contribute to. I know Python and a bit of JavaScript. Something with a friendly maintainer and issues labelled for beginners. I also want to write a short blog post about the whole experience once I've done it, maybe by the end of the month.
Look at projects with a 'good first issue' label and an active maintainer. Documentation fixes are a gentle start.
I'll start with documentation fixes and write the blog post after my first merged pull request.
